---
name: aws-design-review
description: Create and review AWS design sheets. Approve which ARP4-parsed documents a design may cite, generate design workbooks from structured input, and review them through a prioritised review pack with required-input gaps, declared project policies, optional local AWS static checks and CFN comparison. Also review documented line-format design text or saved checker JSON. Use for AWS design generation and review, not deployment or direct Office/PDF extraction.
---

# AWS design review

This `SKILL.md` directory is the package root. Keep `pyproject.toml`, `src/`, `schemas/`, `profiles/`, and `rules/` together. Use the installed CLI in this directory's `.venv`, with absolute input/output paths when running from another working directory. If installation is needed, use `scripts/install.ps1` on Windows; dependencies come from PyPI. The installer first lists earlier installations: this copy's existing `.venv`, older-version `aws-design-review` copies in the `.claude`, `.agents`, `.github` and `.codex` skill folders of this project and of the user profile, and `aws-design-sheet` installed into the Python it uses. Copies of the same or a newer version are kept. It moves the listed folders to the Recycle Bin and uninstalls the package only after confirmation; a removed copy's schema cache goes with it. Run it without `-Force` first. When it stops with the list, show the list to the user and rerun with `-Force` only after they approve those removals. Do not enable optional LLM extraction without the user's request. Commands and contracts are in [references/usage.md](references/usage.md); the detailed reporting rules for each result type are in [references/reporting.md](references/reporting.md).

Initial setup downloads the official Tokyo, Osaka and us-east-1 CloudFormation schemas (network access, no AWS credentials, no AWS account operations). Before reporting setup, drift or regional review results, read "Schema setup and regional reviews" in [references/reporting.md](references/reporting.md).

## Start here

1. Run `aws-design flow status --workspace WS --markdown` (create the workspace with `aws-design flow init` if absent). To let agents take routine decisions, offer a delegation policy once: `aws-design delegation init --output WS/delegation/policy.json`, show it with `aws-design delegation show`, and have the person the user names approve it (`aws-design delegation approve … --output WS/delegation/approval.json`).
2. Loop on `aws-design flow run all --workspace WS` and its `next`: it performs scans, generation, gates and every DELEGATED decision itself and stops at the first step that needs someone. Run the read-only commands (`check`, `show`, `diff`, `suggest`, `compare`, `recall`, `status`, `aws-design contract validate`, `aws-design gate run`) whenever useful.
3. WAITING_FOR_AGENT: start the named agent (`aws-design-author` or `aws-design-checker`, see "Agents") as many times as `count` says, each a separate run with a different actor name, given exactly the handoff with its `role` and `instructions` (when the handoff lists `runs`, run N also gets the Nth entry: its own output, check, actor and the file it must not read); do not let runs see each other's outputs. Validate what it writes with `aws-design contract validate` and send failures back to that run, then loop again. When the named agent is `aws-design-review`, the work is yours, in this session: a failing gate (read `aws-design gate run --workspace WS --markdown`) or unclassified open settings; fix your handover in a new copy of the input, point flow.json at it and loop.
4. WAITING_FOR_PERSON: the decision is outside the approved policy. Stop, show the user the command, the role and `delegation_refused`, and run it only with the person the user names, never with your own name; offer `aws-design flow inbox` when several are pending. When the user names the people for each role, register them once with `aws-design flow people`.
5. Open decisions go to people one decision at a time. When you mark a setting UNDECIDED, say why with `cause`: OWNER_DECISION (the owner decides), WAITS_FOR (decided after a known event such as a test), EXTERNAL_DATA (a value supplied from outside), DESIGNER_TASK (the designer works it out later) or BUILD_NOTE (decided or fixed at build time, or left open only by the tool or the input's form, for example a property the tool refuses as a secret); the first three also name the decision with `ask` (one ID for every setting one answer decides). A value the documents decide but the tool cannot hold is OMITTED or UNDECIDED with cause BUILD_NOTE, never asked. The asks ledger is the one way the design asks people (a workspace made with `aws-design flow init --no-asks` asks nobody): the flow asks an `aws-design-author` in the role `ask-drafter` for the ledger and an `aws-design-checker` in the role `ask-reviewer` to review it, sends the ready decisions in order as one short sheet per audience and a meeting agenda (`aws-design asks sheet`), and applies recorded answers to a new copy of the input (`aws-design asks apply`). The ledger also carries, as decisions without settings, the system overview's open questions and missing quality targets and defaults that need confirming; the designer writes those answers into the overview or the input. Answers are recorded only for the people who gave them: show `aws-design asks record … --dry-run` first so the user sees what each answer will set. Never answer an ask, and never ask people what the documents decide, what the designer works out or what only the tool's form left open.
6. Explain results from the latest `runs/NNN/review-pack.md` (see "Report results"). When the organisation has its own design-sheet workbook, fill a copy with `aws-design export` and a mapping file instead of handing over the tool's own workbook.

## Machine-checked handovers

Every file an agent or person hands over has a contract (`aws-design contract list`, `schema --kind K`, JSON Schemas in `schemas/contracts`). Each generation writes `runs/NNN/gates.json`: contracts of every workspace file, the source set, grounding (each document value is found in the cells it cites; a cell citation that does not hold its value or a literal with no source fails), a grounding self-test with a planted value, the diagram coverage, overview conflicts and the generation itself. FAIL stops the flow; WARN (values cited only by sheet or document, or citations outside ARP4) continues and stays visible. Cite the exact cells (`DOCUMENT_ID#s1-C5`) so values are GROUNDED, not merely found in a document. The diagram coverage (`runs/NNN/diagram-coverage.md`) joins the reviewed diagram ledger with the input: it fails while a drawing of a CURRENT document has no disposition, a resource, actor, account, environment, VPC, subnet or line the ledger maps is cited by nothing in the input, a resource sits outside the account, environment, region, zone, VPC or subnet its frames show, several icons are folded into one resource or actor (one resource drawn once in each subnet or zone it uses, such as an ECS service spread over two zones, is not folding when its subnets hold every icon), a diagram document contributes nothing, or the ledger lacks an independent review. 100 % coverage means every element has a target or an explicit disposition, not that every element became an AWS resource.

## Delegated decisions

An approved delegation policy (`delegation/policy.json` with `delegation/approval.json` binding its hash, by a person) lets `aws-design flow run all` record, under `agent:aws-design flow` with the policy hash, the rule and the evidence: a source-set proposal without UNDECIDED documents or source issues; an overview agreement when two independent drafts agree, an independent review accepted and the findings are within the policy; adoption of the policy packs it names; OK for P2 review rows that every independent `review-pack-checker` run passed while catching every planted canary row. `aws-design external agree --workspace WS` approves mapping proposals two independent readings make identically. A changed policy, a suspended rule or a failing gate leaves the step to people. `aws-design delegation audit sample|record` lets a person check a sample of agent decisions; `aws-design delegation calibrate [--golden REPORT]` suspends rules whose audits, canaries or `aws-design golden score` results fall short. P1 rows, workbook changes, library promotion and the policy itself always stay with people.

## Decisions that belong to a named person

| Decision | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Which ARP4 documents are CURRENT, SUPERSEDED, REFERENCE or EXCLUDED | `aws-design sources approve … --approver NAME [--set DOCUMENT_ID=STATUS]` |
| Agreeing the system overview before design sheets | `aws-design system approve OVERVIEW --approver NAME --output FILE` |
| Adopting a policy pack such as `aws-security-baseline` | `aws-design policy-pack apply … --adopted-by NAME` |
| Mapping proposals of an external sheet | `aws-design external approve … --approver NAME` |
| Answers to the asks of a design (a choice, a value, a hold with its reason, or that what an ask waits for happened) | `aws-design asks record … --by NAME` (after `--dry-run`) or `aws-design asks ready --ask ID --by NAME` |
| Review verdicts the reviewer wrote as OK/NG in `review-pack.xlsx` or exported from `review-pack.html` | `aws-design review-pack record … --reviewer NAME` or `aws-design review-pack import --file …` |
| Applying workbook edit proposals from `aws-design changes propose` | `aws-design changes apply` with an approver |
| Promoting a project's approved dictionary entries to the organisation library | `aws-design library promote … --promoter NAME` |
| Approving the delegation policy that lets agents take the decisions above within its rules | `aws-design delegation approve POLICY --approver NAME --output FILE` |
| Auditing a sample of agent decisions | `aws-design delegation audit record --workspace WS --workbook … --auditor NAME` |

These are a person's decisions unless the approved delegation policy covers them, in which case only `aws-design flow run all` (or `aws-design external agree`) records them, under an agent name. When several decisions are pending, offer `aws-design flow inbox` so the people fill one workbook, and record it with `aws-design flow decide` (names come from the workbook or the registered roles). Never fill the decision or person columns yourself. Never approve, adopt, review or apply as the agent, pass an `agent:` name to a person's command (the CLI refuses it), write a decision record by hand, mark a policy declaration CONFIRMED yourself, or review an items file you wrote. The `aws-design-checker` runs record their own reviews of another agent's work; that is their role, not an approval of the design.

## Never

- Deploy AWS resources, run AWS account operations, install cloud credentials, or fetch secret references.
- Invent physical IDs, account IDs, defaults, expected policy values or sources, or infer executable policies from prose.
- Upload the user's source or result files. Outputs stay in the user's chosen location.
- Edit source inputs or design files a person wrote unless the user asks (fix your own handover in a new copy and point flow.json at it), silently reinterpret prose as line-format input, or enable optional LLM extraction without the user's request.
- Put secret values in inputs (they use secret references) or copy cell values into agent text.
- Reuse an output directory: every run goes to a fresh one.

## Choose the input contract

- ARP4-parsed documents (drafts, copies and archived versions sit side by side): settle the source set first with `aws-design sources scan --arp-root ROOT --output FRESH_FILE` (the flow does this), and let the flow approve it under the delegation policy or show the user `aws-design sources show --source-set FILE` and have the approver decide. Before asking for that approval, read the title and cover of every document proposed CURRENT or UNDECIDED (the table's 表題・位置付け column, or its first cells through ARP4) and name each one that is not a design basis (a proposal, estimate, RFP, another project's or a vendor's material), recommending `--set DOCUMENT_ID=REFERENCE` or `EXCLUDED`; POSSIBLY_REFERENCE rows already name the cells that suggest it. Never call a proposal fine as proposed without that reading. If, while writing the input, you decide a CURRENT document must not be a basis, do not just leave it uncited: ask the approver to change its status (a fresh scan and approval), because a CURRENT document the design ignores is a decision nobody recorded. Then read and cite only CURRENT documents (source `locator`: `DOCUMENT_ID#s1-C5` for cells, `DOCUMENT_ID#シート名` or `DOCUMENT_ID` only when no cell holds the value). Generation with `--source-set SET --arp-root ROOT` stops on SOURCE_SET_FAILED, and `aws-design external` takes `--source-set` too.
- System overview, before any design sheet: the system above AWS resources (requirements, actors, boundaries, components, data flows, quality targets, open questions) in its own file. Start it from the ARP4 registry with `aws-design system init --arp-root ROOT --source-set SET …` (add `--template NAME [--library LIB]` when a typical shape fits; its elements start UNDECIDED), fill in what the documents say, run `aws-design system check OVERVIEW [--design INPUT] --output DIR` and show `system-overview.md`. Never invent components, flows, targets or links the documents do not state: leave them UNDECIDED or as open questions. Add its decided requirements to the 1.1 input with `aws-design system design-requirements`. With `aws-design flow init --overview`, the flow asks an `aws-design-author` in the role `overview-drafter` (twice when the delegation policy requires a second, independent draft) and an `aws-design-checker` in the role `overview-reviewer`; the agreement is then recorded by the flow under the policy or goes to the person the user names.
- Structured generation input (`schema_version` 1.0 or 1.1 with `system`, `environments`, `resources`): `aws-design document INPUT --environment ENV --output FRESH_DIRECTORY` creates the workbooks, the required-input checklist, the collection matrix and the review pack. Confirm only missing environment/output choices that cannot be inferred. When you write a 1.1 input from documents, follow "Write a design input from documents" below. Add `--evaluate` when asked to evaluate AWS validity; it is local static analysis and needs no AWS credentials. Optional `--cfn FILE` compares declared bindings and never fills missing values.
- Project requirements: explicit `project_policies` declarations run during generation; `required_inputs` describes presence obligations and `project_policies` compares known values. A standard set goes into a new input with `aws-design policy-pack apply`.
- External Excel design sheet parsed by ARP4 (`extraction.json`, `document.yml`, accepted structure): give the cell reading to two `aws-design-author` runs in the role `sheet-extract-worker` with different actor names that do not see each other's file (each writes an items file citing cell IDs, starting from `aws-design external suggest`), run `aws-design external compare`, and give the review of the first reading to an `aws-design-checker` in the role `sheet-extract-reviewer`, which starts from the disagreeing cells and records the review; `aws-design external agree --workspace WS` approves the proposals both readings make identically under the delegation policy and the approver the user names approves the rest, and `build` writes a 1.1 input and `source-trace.json` for `--source-trace` (set it in flow.json so its values count as TRACED in the grounding gate). ARP4 is not bundled.
- Documents that draw (architecture diagrams, icons, connectors, pasted images): the goal is not a tidy overview but that nothing the CURRENT documents draw is lost. Before the input is written, the flow asks two `aws-design-author` runs in the role `diagram-extract-worker` per document for independent readings (`diagrams/parts/<document>/ledger.json` and `reading-2.json`; a workspace that already has `diagrams/ledger.json` keeps one ledger for all documents) that give every drawing one disposition by reference (`s1-d4`), and an `aws-design-checker` in the role `diagram-extract-reviewer` to review each first reading after `aws-design diagram compare`. When a handoff lists `runs`, start one agent per run (in batches if there are many); each part is read, reviewed and read again on its own. A document that draws nothing of the system may be set aside as a whole (`scope: NOT_ARCHITECTURE`) instead of an entry per element, but only when both readings and the review say so. When one reading of a part fails and the other passes, `aws-design diagram adopt --workspace WS --document D` makes the passing one the reading the design uses and keeps the failed one in `retired/` with a record; `retire` takes a reading out of use so a fresh one is written to a new file. Never overwrite or delete a reading by hand. Before handing off the workers, run the handoff's `preflight` (`aws-design diagram preflight`): it lists per document the pictures without text, alternative text or graph, lines whose ends only an image shows, and documents whose ARP4 structure is not accepted, before any costly reading starts. A picture without text that draws part of the system is read in ARP4 before the workers start, so both read the same accepted structure: render its range (`arp4 spec structure render`), open the PNG, record what it shows as the visual's graph with `reading.method: vision`, and have the ARP4 structure reviewed; a worker that meets such a picture without a graph stops and reports it. Give each graph edge only a label the image shows, and none to a line without text. What cannot be read is UNRESOLVED with an ask, never deleted. Nothing in the ledger is settled design information until its review is accepted.
- Documented line-format text: `aws-design run`. Saved checker intermediate JSON: `aws-design check`; generated `design.json` is a different contract.
- Free prose or Office/PDF: explain the supported contracts. This package does not read Office or PDF files. Optional Anthropic extraction (`--extractor llm`) sends the text to an external API, needs separate credentials and may incur charges; use it only when the user asks.

## Agents

Two agents do the work the flow hands off; what each run does is its `role`, whose instructions are in [references/roles/](references/roles/) and named in the handoff's `instructions`.

| Agent | Roles | Writes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `aws-design-author` | `overview-drafter`, `ask-drafter`, `sheet-extract-worker`, `diagram-extract-worker` | the overview draft, `asks/ledger.json`, an external sheet's items file, a diagram ledger |
| `aws-design-checker` | `overview-reviewer`, `ask-reviewer`, `sheet-extract-reviewer`, `diagram-extract-reviewer`, `review-pack-checker` | a review recorded through the CLI, or a review pack verdicts file |

A checker never checks what it wrote, and two runs that must be independent never see each other's files. Codex has no agent definitions: run each role in a separate session under its own actor name, reading the same instructions file. The P2 rows of a review pack go to `review-pack-checker` runs as the flow asks; P1 rows always go to people.

## Write a design input from documents

- Cite the cell that holds each value. A value you derive (a time-zone or unit conversion, a word turned into a flag or an enum, a count from a description) cites that cell and says in `rationale` how it was derived; the grounding gate counts it INTERPRETED and the review pack gives it to a person. `decision_ids` links a value to the decision it realizes and never replaces its citation. When you report the input, give the GROUNDED and INTERPRETED counts and never call derived values quoted from the documents.
- A setting a document states for one scope (a chapter, a table, a kind of resource) applies to that scope only. Resources outside it get the setting UNDECIDED with cause DESIGNER_TASK and a rationale naming the scope whose value might fit; never copy it across.
- Leave no silent gaps. When the documents do not give something a property needs, that setting, or that `$design` leaf of a COMPOSITE value, is UNDECIDED with its cause; a rationale saying "not written" beside a decided value is a gap left out. Before handing over, generate once and settle every MISSING row of `checklist.json` and the review pack (required properties, such as `DistributionConfig.Enabled` of a CloudFront distribution): cite the value or mark it UNDECIDED.
- Write every value the documents give even when a related feature cannot be modelled: the minimum task count is an ECS service's `DesiredCount` although its Application Auto Scaling stays a decision. A type the catalog lacks stays a decision and becomes an `actors` entry of kind AWS_SERVICE, so that its flows can be drawn.
- Declare every flow the documents describe as a TRAFFIC connection, including those with people, outside systems (identity providers, payment services, mail recipients) and AWS services outside the catalog, which are `actors` (USER, OPERATOR, EXTERNAL_SYSTEM, AWS_SERVICE). A connection's protocol and ports state only what the documents decide: when the setting behind them is open, leave them out or mark the connection UNDECIDED.
- Use `operations` for operation and recovery notes the documents state (planned outages, backup and restore procedures), so the workbook's 運用復旧 sheet is not empty.
- With a reviewed diagram ledger, map every element it marks RESOURCE, ACTOR, CONNECTION, or BOUNDARY of an account, environment, VPC or subnet by citing it in that object's own `sources` (`DOCUMENT_ID#s1-d4`, or `#v:VISUAL/n:NODE` for what was read from an image). Each icon is its own resource: the same service drawn in another account, environment, region, zone or for another purpose is another resource, and you never fold icons into one resource or a "services" actor on your own judgment. Only a DUPLICATE element may share its original's target.
- Place each resource as its frames say: declare the accounts (`accounts`, an environment's `account`, a resource's `account`), list `environments` on a resource that exists only in some of them, set `region`, and reference the subnets and VPCs the frames show. A detailed input comes first; a summary drawing is derived from it, never a substitute.

## Report results

1. `review-pack.md`: P1 decisions first, then P2 interpretations, the P3 sample and the P4 count. Each row carries its provenance and the original text it was read from.
2. `collection-matrix.md`: rows to review, source flags and current documents never cited.
3. `summary.json`, `checklist.json`, optional `project-policy.json` and optional `evaluation.json`. Report separately the generation status, CFN comparison, `input_completeness`, `project_policy_status`/`project_policy_assessment`, `evaluation_status`/`aws_assessment` and `source_set_status`.
4. `diagram-coverage.md` when the documents draw: the counts per disposition, the coverage and every finding, and separately the AWS service types, logical resources and placements (a resource in each environment it exists in, by account, environment, region and zone). `architecture.drawio` has a page per account, region and environment when there are several.
5. `gates.json` of the run and the decisions agents recorded (`aws-design delegation status`, `delegation/log`): say which decisions were delegated, under which rule, and which went to people and why (`delegation_refused`, `agent-review/escalation.json`).
6. For version 1.1, ground the explanation in `review-report.json` and `review-report.md`: report `source_review` (a source's transcribed approval and item reviews, never an approval inferred from DECIDED), `rule_review_causes` and `external_bindings` (local values, not verified AWS state) separately, and keep unbound source symbols apart from RESOURCE_REF, APP from AWS scope and CLI execution from actual-host acceptance. With `decisions` or `design_outline`, also read `decision-trace.json` and `basic-design.md`: report `design_decision_assessment` and GAP/CONFLICT/OPEN findings, trace only explicit `decision_ids`/`policy_ids`/`applies_to`, never call REALIZED a policy approval, and report EXPANSION_OVERRIDDEN as an exception. For workbook edits use `aws-design changes propose`, and run `apply` only with an approver the user names.

GENERATED, COMPLETE, DONE, PASS, a passing gate, a delegated decision and P4 describe execution, machine checks or review order, not a person's approval. Exit 0 can include FAIL findings; exit 2 means input, configuration or output errors; exit 3 means an evaluator failed or AWS evaluation was skipped as unsupported. Do not hide those failures.

Give each relevant finding's ID, resource/property, condition, source and input pointer. Report missing, unknown, undecided, referenced and unregistered requirements explicitly. Exceptions are EXEMPTED, not PASS. Even COMPLIANT_WITHIN_DECLARED_SCOPE does not establish whole-requirement coverage. BlockPublicAcls=false by itself does not prove public access. Never equate CFN equality, an empty findings list, a source-set PASS or a generated workbook with deployment safety or complete collection.

Before reporting gates or delegated decisions, source-set codes, system-overview findings, verdicts, version 1.1 traces and decisions, project policies, schema setup or regional reviews, external-sheet imports, or line-format and checker results, read the matching section of [reporting.md](references/reporting.md).
